reference_title: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures, 1993 Edition
chapter_title: Part I, Chapter 1 -- Introduction and Background

sections.title: Scope of the Guide
sections.summary: The Guide provides comprehensive design/rehabilitation procedures for rigid (PCC) and flexible (AC) pavements and aggregate-surfaced low-volume roads, including total and individual layer thicknesses. Part I is general background; Part II covers new/reconstructed pavement design; Part III covers rehabilitation (with or without overlay); Part IV summarizes mechanistic-empirical design status.
sections.body: This Guide for the Design of Pavement Structures provides a comprehensive set of procedures for the design and rehabilitation of pavements: both rigid (PCC surface) and flexible (AC surface), plus aggregate-surfaced roads for low-volume applications, as illustrated conceptually (Figure 1.1, referenced). Recommendations cover total pavement structure thickness as well as individual structural component thicknesses, for a variety of materials and construction procedures. A glossary of terms is provided in Appendix A (AASHTO definitions used where possible, though local practice may differ). Part I provides general background/interpretive material for the design procedures and concepts (economic evaluation, reliability, drainage, life-cycle costs, traffic, pavement type selection); detailed information on specific design considerations is in the Appendices, with references following each of the four Parts. Part II provides the detailed method for new pavement design or reconstruction on the existing alignment (with new or recycled materials). Part III provides alternative rehabilitation methods with or without an overlay, developed to be broadly applicable across overlay type combinations (flexible-on-rigid, flexible-on-flexible, rigid-on-rigid, rigid-on-flexible) and consistent with Part II's performance/design concepts (drainage, reliability, traffic all treated the same for new and rehabilitated pavements).
key_points: Comprehensive design/rehabilitation procedures for rigid, flexible, and aggregate-surfaced (low-volume) pavements
Part II: design of new pavements / reconstruction
Part III: rehabilitation with or without overlay (broadly applicable across overlay-type combinations)
Part IV: mechanistic-empirical design state-of-knowledge summary
sections.applicability: Orientation to the Guide's overall structure before applying Part II design procedures.

sections.title: Design Considerations
sections.summary: Notes that pavement design involves more than layer-thickness selection: material requirements, construction requirements, and quality control significantly influence whether the constructed pavement performs to design expectations; special provisions should address nonstandard conditions (e.g. expansive/nonstandard roadbed soils).
sections.body: Total-set considerations required to assure reliable pavement performance extend beyond thickness design: material requirements, construction requirements, and quality control significantly influence a pavement's ability to perform as expected. A good designer must be familiar with relevant AASHTO/ASTM publications and local agency practice, and should prepare special provisions when nonstandard conditions exist for a specific project (e.g. a roadbed soil known to be expansive or otherwise nonstandard, or materials requiring stabilization for use in the pavement structure or prepared roadbed).
key_points: Pavement design involves more than choosing thicknesses
Material requirements, construction requirements, and quality control significantly affect performance
Special provisions needed for nonstandard conditions (e.g. expansive roadbed soils)
sections.applicability: General framing for how the numeric design procedures fit within the broader pavement delivery process.

sections.title: Shoulder Design
sections.summary: Shoulder design (tied concrete shoulders or widened lanes for rigid pavements is a major new 1993 Guide consideration) is addressed via a position paper in Appendix E; not digitized as callable functions in this module.
sections.body: The 1993 revision added treatment of tied concrete shoulders or widened outside lanes as one of its 14 major new considerations (see the Preface). Appendix E ('Position Paper on Shoulder Design') provides the supporting discussion; this module does not digitize shoulder-design content as callable functions.
key_points: Tied PCC shoulders / widened lanes is one of the 14 major 1993-Guide additions
Appendix E: Position Paper on Shoulder Design (not digitized in this module)
sections.applicability: Background pointer to Appendix E; the rigid pavement structural design chapter (Section 3.4.3, transverse reinforcement / tied shoulders) has the numeric J-factor treatment (Table 2.6).
